Agent Name: Planner
, Step Number: 14
, Reason for Mistake: In Step 14, the Planner incorrectly analyzed the WebSurfer results from the previous turn. The WebSurfer had found a Wikidata link in the search results, but the Planner's analysis claimed that "No birthplace value was extracted from the visible portion" and that the birthplace was unknown, failing to notice that the search result snippet itself (visible in the previous turn's viewport) clearly stated "(22 September 1869, Évreux - 9 December 1925, Paris)" and linked to a page where this data exists. More critically, in the *very next* step (which is part of the same logical error sequence initiated by the Planner's misinterpretation of the available data), the Planner instructs the WebSurfer to open the BnF link and claims that the BnF source lists the birthplace as **Paris**, whereas the BnF entry (and all other reliable sources like Deutsche Biographie and Wikidata) actually lists **Évreux**. The Planner hallucinated that the BnF source said Paris, leading the team to believe there was a conflict between Évreux and Paris, when in reality, all authoritative sources point to Évreux. This misinterpretation of the search results and the hallucination of the BnF content caused the team to pursue unnecessary verification and ultimately fail to confirm the correct answer (Évreux) based on the evidence already present.
